editorial.headline: Scaffolding Installation: Open Nationally, Clear of Bali’s PMA Moratorium
editorial.standfirst: This specialised scaffolding-installation activity spans sites from buildings to wharves, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block recorded.
editorial.body:
Scaffolding installation sits at a precise point in the construction process: the specialised placement of scaffolding or steger. Under this activity, the work can be carried out on buildings, roads and bridges, waterworks, wharves, and comparable sites. The scope is defined by the installation itself and by the range of structures on which it is performed. It also identifies PL008 as the associated scaffolding-installation sub-classification. For a founder choosing an activity, that specificity is the essential starting point: the recorded work is scaffolding installation across those listed built environments.

Eligibility is not confined to one business size. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, placing the same defined activity within the full sequence of sizes recorded here. That breadth should be read alongside the scope, rather than as an invitation to stretch it: the point remains the specialised installation of scaffolding on the listed categories of site. The scale entry says who may register it; the scope says what they register for.

Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA and the recorded maximum foreign ownership is 100%. In plain terms, the national record permits PMA participation up to a 100% foreign ownership ceiling for this activity. Bali must be read separately. Its province-wide, permanent moratorium blocks PMA registrations for every KBLI classified Low or Medium-Low risk. That is a regulatory screen, not a rhetorical footnote, and it cannot be ignored merely because national ownership is open.

Here, however, the Bali record does not mark the activity as blocked. At the Large scale, its OSS risk is recorded as Medium-High or High, so it is not blocked by that moratorium. The Bali result is therefore genuinely open for PMA registration for this code: there is no moratorium block recorded. The most accurate reading holds both levels together: national PMA openness with a 100% ceiling, and a Bali assessment that allows this activity past the island-wide Low and Medium-Low risk restriction.
